[takes care of finding a random port available on your local machine which is assigned to the new](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html#method.start)

`start`[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`To ensure full isolation and no cross-test interference, [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)s shouldn't be
shared between tests. Instead,

[s should be created in the test where they are used.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`When a [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance goes out of scope (e.g. the test finishes), the corresponding
HTTP server running in the background is shut down to free up the port it was using.

## Runtime compatibility

`wiremock` can be used (and it is tested to work) with both [ async_std](https://docs.rs/async-std/) and

[as futures runtimes. If you encounter any compatibility bug, please open an issue on our](https://docs.rs/tokio/)

`tokio`[GitHub repository](https://github.com/LukeMathWalker/wiremock-rs).

## Efficiency

`wiremock` maintains a pool of mock servers in the background to minimise the number of
connections and the time spent starting up a new [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html).
Pooling reduces the likelihood of you having to tune your OS configurations (e.g. ulimit).

The pool is designed to be invisible: it makes your life easier and your tests faster. If you end up having to worry about it, it's a bug: open an issue!

## Prior art

[ mockito](https://docs.rs/mockito/) and

[provide HTTP mocking for Rust.](https://docs.rs/httpmock/)

`httpmock`Check the table below to see how `wiremock` compares to them across the following dimensions:

- Test execution strategy (do tests have to be executed sequentially or can they be executed in parallel?);
- How many APIs can I mock in a test?
- Out-of-the-box request matchers;
- Extensible request matching (i.e. you can define your own matchers);
- Sync/Async API;
- Spying (e.g. verify that a mock has/hasn't been called in a test);
- Standalone mode (i.e. can I launch an HTTP mock server outside of a test suite?).

| Test execution strategy | How many APIs can I mock? | Out-of-the-box request matchers | Extensible request matching | API | Spying | Standalone mode | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mockito | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ❌ |
| httpmock | ✔ Parallel | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async/Sync | ✔ | ✔ |
| wiremock | ✔ Parallel ️ | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async | ✔ | ❌ |

## Future evolution

More request matchers can be added to those provided out-of-the-box to handle common usecases.

## Related projects

- `stubr`- `Wiremock`- `MockServer`

`wiremock` maintains a pool of mock servers in the background to minimise the number of
connections and the time spent starting up a new [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html).
Pooling reduces the likelihood of you having to tune your OS configurations (e.g. ulimit).

The pool is designed to be invisible: it makes your life easier and your tests faster. If you end up having to worry about it, it's a bug: open an issue!

## Prior art

[ mockito](https://docs.rs/mockito/) and

[provide HTTP mocking for Rust.](https://docs.rs/httpmock/)

`httpmock`Check the table below to see how `wiremock` compares to them across the following dimensions:

- Test execution strategy (do tests have to be executed sequentially or can they be executed in parallel?);
- How many APIs can I mock in a test?
- Out-of-the-box request matchers;
- Extensible request matching (i.e. you can define your own matchers);
- Sync/Async API;
- Spying (e.g. verify that a mock has/hasn't been called in a test);
- Standalone mode (i.e. can I launch an HTTP mock server outside of a test suite?).

| Test execution strategy | How many APIs can I mock? | Out-of-the-box request matchers | Extensible request matching | API | Spying | Standalone mode | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mockito | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ❌ |
| httpmock | ✔ Parallel | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async/Sync | ✔ | ✔ |
| wiremock | ✔ Parallel ️ | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async | ✔ | ❌ |

## Future evolution

More request matchers can be added to those provided out-of-the-box to handle common usecases.

## Related projects

- `stubr`- `Wiremock`- `MockServer`

## Getting started

```

use ;
async
```
## Matchers

`wiremock` provides a set of matching strategies out of the box - check the [ matchers](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/matchers/index.html) module
for a complete list.

You can define your own matchers using the [ Match](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Match.html) trait, as well as using

`Fn` closures.
Check ['s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Match.html)

`Match`## Spying

`wiremock` empowers you to set expectations on the number of invocations to your [ Mock](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)s -
check the

[method for more details.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html#method.expect)

`expect`Expectations can be used to verify that a side-effect has (or has not) taken place!

Expectations are automatically verified during the shutdown of each [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance,
at the end of your test. A failed verification will trigger a panic.
By default, no expectations are set on your

[s.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock`## Responses

`wiremock` lets you specify pre-determined responses using [ ResponseTemplate](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.ResponseTemplate) and

[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockBuilder.html#method.respond_with)

`respond_with`You are also given the option to have [ Mock](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)s return different responses based on the matched

[using the](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Request)

`Request`[trait. Check](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`['s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`## Test isolation

Each instance of [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) is fully isolated:

[takes care of finding a random port available on your local machine which is assigned to the new](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html#method.start)

`start`[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`To ensure full isolation and no cross-test interference, [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)s shouldn't be
shared between tests. Instead,

[s should be created in the test where they are used.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`When a [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance goes out of scope (e.g. the test finishes), the corresponding
HTTP server running in the background is shut down to free up the port it was using.

## Runtime compatibility

`wiremock` can be used (and it is tested to work) with both [ async_std](https://docs.rs/async-std/) and

[as futures runtimes. If you encounter any compatibility bug, please open an issue on our](https://docs.rs/tokio/)

`tokio`[GitHub repository](https://github.com/LukeMathWalker/wiremock-rs).

## Efficiency

`wiremock` maintains a pool of mock servers in the background to minimise the number of
connections and the time spent starting up a new [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html).
Pooling reduces the likelihood of you having to tune your OS configurations (e.g. ulimit).

The pool is designed to be invisible: it makes your life easier and your tests faster. If you end up having to worry about it, it's a bug: open an issue!

| Test execution strategy | How many APIs can I mock? | Out-of-the-box request matchers | Extensible request matching | API | Spying | Standalone mode | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mockito | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ❌ |
| httpmock | ✔ Parallel | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async/Sync | ✔ | ✔ |
| wiremock | ✔ Parallel ️ | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async | ✔ | ❌ |

# wiremock 0.5.10 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wiremock/0.5.10

`wiremock` provides HTTP mocking to perform black-box testing of Rust applications that
interact with third-party APIs.

It provides mocking of HTTP responses using request matching and response templating.

# Table of Contents

```
If you are using [ cargo-edit](https://github.com/killercup/cargo-edit), run

```
```
## Getting started

```
use ;
use ;
async
```
## Matchers

`wiremock` provides a set of matching strategies out of the box - check the [ matchers](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/matchers/index.html) module
for a complete list.

You can define your own matchers using the [ Match](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Match.html) trait, as well as using

`Fn` closures.
Check ['s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Match.html)

`Match`## Spying

`wiremock` empowers you to set expectations on the number of invocations to your [ Mock](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)s -
check the

[method for more details.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html#method.expect)

`expect`Expectations can be used to verify that a side-effect has (or has not) taken place!

Expectations are automatically verified during the shutdown of each [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance,
at the end of your test. A failed verification will trigger a panic.
By default, no expectations are set on your

[s.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock`## Responses

`wiremock` lets you specify pre-determined responses using [ ResponseTemplate](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.ResponseTemplate) and

[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockBuilder.html#method.respond_with)

`respond_with`You are also given the option to have [ Mock](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)s return different responses based on the matched

[using the](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Request)

`Request`[trait. Check](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`['s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`## Test isolation

Each instance of [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) is fully isolated:

[takes care of finding a random port available on your local machine which is assigned to the new](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html#method.start)

`start`[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`To ensure full isolation and no cross-test interference, [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)s shouldn't be
shared between tests. Instead,

[s should be created in the test where they are used.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`When a [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance goes out of scope (e.g. the test finishes), the corresponding
HTTP server running in the background is shut down to free up the port it was using.

## Runtime compatibility

`wiremock` can be used (and it is tested to work) with both [ async_std](https://docs.rs/async-std/) and

[as futures runtimes. If you encounter any compatibility bug, please open an issue on our](https://docs.rs/tokio/)

`tokio`[GitHub repository](https://github.com/LukeMathWalker/wiremock-rs).

## Efficiency

`wiremock` maintains a pool of mock servers in the background to minimise the number of
connections and the time spent starting up a new [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html).
Pooling reduces the likelihood of you having to tune your OS configurations (e.g. ulimit).

The pool is designed to be invisible: it makes your life easier and your tests faster. If you end up having to worry about it, it's a bug: open an issue!

## Prior art

[ mockito](https://docs.rs/mockito/) and

[provide HTTP mocking for Rust.](https://docs.rs/httpmock/)

`httpmock`Check the table below to see how `wiremock` compares to them across the following dimensions:

- Test execution strategy (do tests have to be executed sequentially or can they be executed in parallel?);
- How many APIs can I mock in a test?
- Out-of-the-box request matchers;
- Extensible request matching (i.e. you can define your own matchers);
- Sync/Async API;
- Spying (e.g. verify that a mock has/hasn't been called in a test);
- Standalone mode (i.e. can I launch an HTTP mock server outside of a test suite?).

| Test execution strategy | How many APIs can I mock? | Out-of-the-box request matchers | Extensible request maching | API | Spying | Standalone mode | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mockito | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ❌ |
| httpmock | ✔ Parallel | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async/Sync | ✔ | ✔ |
| wiremock | ✔ Parallel ️ | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async | ✔ | ❌ |

## Future evolution

More request matchers can be added to those provided out-of-the-box to handle common usecases.

# wiremock 0.5.6 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wiremock/0.5.6

`wiremock` provides HTTP mocking to perform black-box testing of Rust applications that
interact with third-party APIs.

It provides mocking of HTTP responses using request matching and response templating.

*The name  wiremock is a reference to  WireMock.Net, a .NET port of the original Wiremock from Java.*

# Table of Contents

- [How to install](https://docs.rs#how-to-install)
- [Getting started](https://docs.rs#getting-started)
- [Matchers](https://docs.rs#matchers)
- [Spying](https://docs.rs#spying)
- [Responses](https://docs.rs#spying)
- [Test isolation](https://docs.rs#test-isolation)
- [Runtime compatibility](https://docs.rs#runtime-compatibility)
- [Efficiency](https://docs.rs#efficiency)
- [Prior art](https://docs.rs#prior-art)
- [Future evolution](https://docs.rs#future-evolution)
- [Related projects](https://docs.rs#related-projects)
- [License](https://docs.rs#license)

## How to install

Add `wiremock` to your development dependencies:

```
[]
# ...
 = "0.5"
```
If you are using [ cargo-edit](https://github.com/killercup/cargo-edit), run

```
```
## Getting started

```
use ;
use ;
async
```
## Matchers

`wiremock` provides a set of matching strategies out of the box - check the [ matchers](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/matchers/index.html) module
for a complete list.

You can define your own matchers using the [ Match](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Match.html) trait, as well as using

`Fn` closures.
Check ['s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Match.html)

`Match`## Spying

`wiremock` empowers you to set expectations on the number of invocations to your [ Mock](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)s -
check the

[method for more details.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html#method.expect)

`expect`Expectations can be used to verify that a side-effect has (or has not) taken place!

Expectations are automatically verified during the shutdown of each [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance,
at the end of your test. A failed verification will trigger a panic.
By default, no expectations are set on your

[s.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock`## Responses

`wiremock` lets you specify pre-determined responses using [ ResponseTemplate](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.ResponseTemplate) and

[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockBuilder.html#method.respond_with)

`respond_with`You are also given the option to have [ Mock](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)s return different responses based on the matched

[using the](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Request)

`Request`[trait. Check](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`['s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`## Test isolation

Each instance of [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) is fully isolated:

[takes care of finding a random port available on your local machine which is assigned to the new](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html#method.start)

`start`[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`To ensure full isolation and no cross-test interference, [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)s shouldn't be
shared between tests. Instead,

[s should be created in the test where they are used.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`When a [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance goes out of scope (e.g. the test finishes), the corresponding
HTTP server running in the background is shut down to free up the port it was using.

## Runtime compatibility

`wiremock` can be used (and it is tested to work) with both [ async_std](https://docs.rs/async-std/) and

[as futures runtimes. If you encounter any compatibility bug, please open an issue on our](https://docs.rs/tokio/)

`tokio`[GitHub repository](https://github.com/LukeMathWalker/wiremock-rs).

## Efficiency

`wiremock` maintains a pool of mock servers in the background to minimise the number of
connections and the time spent starting up a new [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html).
Pooling reduces the likelihood of you having to tune your OS configurations (e.g. ulimit).

The pool is designed to be invisible: it makes your life easier and your tests faster. If you end up having to worry about it, it's a bug: open an issue!

## Prior art

[ mockito](https://docs.rs/mockito/) and

[provide HTTP mocking for Rust.](https://docs.rs/httpmock/)

`httpmock`Check the table below to see how `wiremock` compares to them across the following dimensions:

- Test execution strategy (do tests have to be executed sequentially or can they be executed in parallel?);
- How many APIs can I mock in a test?
- Out-of-the-box request matchers;
- Extensible request matching (i.e. you can define your own matchers);
- Sync/Async API;
- Spying (e.g. verify that a mock has/hasn't been called in a test);
- Standalone mode (i.e. can I launch an HTTP mock server outside of a test suite?).

| Test execution strategy | How many APIs can I mock? | Out-of-the-box request matchers | Extensible request maching | API | Spying | Standalone mode | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mockito | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ❌ |
| httpmock | ✔ Parallel | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async/Sync | ✔ | ✔ |
| wiremock | ✔ Parallel ️ | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async | ✔ | ❌ |

## Future evolution

More request matchers can be added to those provided out-of-the-box to handle common usecases.

## Related projects

- `stubr`- `Wiremock`- `MockServer`

## License

Licensed under either of Apache License, Version 2.0 or MIT license at your option. Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in this crate by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

If you are using [ cargo-edit](https://github.com/killercup/cargo-edit), run

```
```
## Getting started

```
use ;
use ;
async
```
## Matchers

`wiremock` provides a set of matching strategies out of the box - check the [ matchers](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/matchers/index.html) module
for a complete list.

You can define your own matchers using the [ Match](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Match.html) trait, as well as using

`Fn` closures.
Check ['s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Match.html)

`Match`## Spying

`wiremock` empowers you to set expectations on the number of invocations to your [ Mock](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)s -
check the

[method for more details.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html#method.expect)

`expect`Expectations can be used to verify that a side-effect has (or has not) taken place!

Expectations are automatically verified during the shutdown of each [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance,
at the end of your test. A failed verification will trigger a panic.
By default, no expectations are set on your

[s.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock`## Responses

`wiremock` lets you specify pre-determined responses using [ ResponseTemplate](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.ResponseTemplate) and

[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockBuilder.html#method.respond_with)

`respond_with`You are also given the option to have [ Mock](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)s return different responses based on the matched

[using the](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Request)

`Request`[trait. Check](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`['s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`## Test isolation

Each instance of [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) is fully isolated:

[takes care of finding a random port available on your local machine which is assigned to the new](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html#method.start)

`start`[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`To ensure full isolation and no cross-test interference, [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)s shouldn't be
shared between tests. Instead,

[s should be created in the test where they are used.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`When a [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance goes out of scope (e.g. the test finishes), the corresponding
HTTP server running in the background is shut down to free up the port it was using.

## Runtime compatibility

`wiremock` can be used (and it is tested to work) with both [ async_std](https://docs.rs/async-std/) and

[as futures runtimes. If you encounter any compatibility bug, please open an issue on our](https://docs.rs/tokio/)

`tokio`[GitHub repository](https://github.com/LukeMathWalker/wiremock-rs).

## Efficiency

`wiremock` maintains a pool of mock servers in the background to minimise the number of
connections and the time spent starting up a new [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html).
Pooling reduces the likelihood of you having to tune your OS configurations (e.g. ulimit).

The pool is designed to be invisible: it makes your life easier and your tests faster. If you end up having to worry about it, it's a bug: open an issue!

## Prior art

[ mockito](https://docs.rs/mockito/) and

[provide HTTP mocking for Rust.](https://docs.rs/httpmock/)

`httpmock`Check the table below to see how `wiremock` compares to them across the following dimensions:

- Test execution strategy (do tests have to be executed sequentially or can they be executed in parallel?);
- How many APIs can I mock in a test?
- Out-of-the-box request matchers;
- Extensible request matching (i.e. you can define your own matchers);
- Sync/Async API;
- Spying (e.g. verify that a mock has/hasn't been called in a test);
- Standalone mode (i.e. can I launch an HTTP mock server outside of a test suite?).

| Test execution strategy | How many APIs can I mock? | Out-of-the-box request matchers | Extensible request maching | API | Spying | Standalone mode | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mockito | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ❌ |
| httpmock | ✔ Parallel | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async/Sync | ✔ | ✔ |
| wiremock | ✔ Parallel ️ | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async | ✔ | ❌ |

## Future evolution

More request matchers can be added to those provided out-of-the-box to handle common usecases.

## Related projects

- `stubr`- `Wiremock`- `MockServer`

Check ['s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/trait.Match.html)

`Match`## Spying

`wiremock` empowers you to set expectations on the number of invocations to your [ Mock](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)s -
check the

[method for more details.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.Mock.html#method.expect)

`expect`Expectations can be used to verify that a side-effect has (or has not) taken place!

Expectations are automatically verified during the shutdown of each [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance,
at the end of your test. A failed verification will trigger a panic.
By default, no expectations are set on your

[s.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock`## Responses

`wiremock` lets you specify pre-determined responses using [ ResponseTemplate](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.ResponseTemplate) and

[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockBuilder.html#method.respond_with)

`respond_with`You also given the option to have [ Mock](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)s that return different responses based on the matched

[using the](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.Request)

`Request`[trait. Check](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`['s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`## Test isolation

Each instance of [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) is fully isolated:

[takes care of finding a random port available on your local machine which is assigned to the new](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html#method.start)

`start`[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`To ensure full isolation and no cross-test interference, [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)s shouldn't be
shared between tests. Instead,

[s should be created in the test where they are used.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`When a [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance goes out of scope (e.g. the test finishes), the corresponding
HTTP server running in the background is shut down to free up the port it was using.

## Runtime compatibility

`wiremock` can be used (and it is tested to work) with both [ async_std](https://docs.rs/async-std/) and

[as futures runtimes. If you encounter any compatibility bug, please open an issue on our](https://docs.rs/tokio/)

`tokio`[GitHub repository](https://github.com/LukeMathWalker/wiremock-rs).

## Efficiency

`wiremock` maintains a pool of mock servers in the background to minimise the number of
connections and the time spent starting up a new [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html).
Pooling reduces the likelihood of you having to tune your OS configurations (e.g. ulimit).

The pool is designed to be invisible: it makes your life easier and your tests faster. If you end up having to worry about it, it's a bug: open an issue!

## Prior art

[ mockito](https://docs.rs/mockito/) and

[provide HTTP mocking for Rust.](https://docs.rs/httpmock/)

`httpmock`Check the table below to see how `wiremock` compares to them across the following dimensions:

- Test execution strategy (do tests have to be executed sequentially or can they be executed in parallel?);
- How many APIs can I mock in a test?
- Out-of-the-box request matchers;
- Extensible request matching (i.e. you can define your own matchers);
- Sync/Async API;
- Spying (e.g. verify that a mock has/hasn't been called in a test);
- Standalone mode (i.e. can I launch an HTTP mock server outside of a test suite?).

| Test execution strategy | How many APIs can I mock? | Out-of-the-box request matchers | Extensible request maching | API | Spying | Standalone mode | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mockito | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ❌ |
| httpmock | ✔ Parallel | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async/Sync | ✔ | ✔ |
| wiremock | ✔ Parallel ️ | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async | ✔ | ❌ |

## Future evolution

More request matchers can be added to those provided out-of-the-box to handle common usecases.

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in this crate by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

`expect`Expectations can be used to verify that a side-effect has (or has not) taken place!

Expectations are automatically verified during the shutdown of each [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance,
at the end of your test. A failed verification will trigger a panic.
By default, no expectations are set on your

[s.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock`## Responses

`wiremock` lets you specify pre-determined responses using [ ResponseTemplate](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.ResponseTemplate) and

[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockBuilder.html#method.respond_with)

`respond_with`You also given the option to have [ Mock](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)s that return different responses based on the matched

[using the](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.Request)

`Request`[trait. Check](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`['s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`## Test isolation

Each instance of [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) is fully isolated:

[takes care of finding a random port available on your local machine which is assigned to the new](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html#method.start)

`start`[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`To ensure full isolation and no cross-test interference, [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)s shouldn't be
shared between tests. Instead,

[s should be created in the test where they are used.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`When a [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance goes out of scope (e.g. the test finishes), the corresponding
HTTP server running in the background is shut down to free up the port it was using.

## Runtime compatibility

`wiremock` can be used (and it is tested to work) with both [ async_std](https://docs.rs/async-std/) and

[as futures runtimes. If you encounter any compatibility bug, please open an issue on our](https://docs.rs/tokio/)

`tokio`[GitHub repository](https://github.com/LukeMathWalker/wiremock-rs).

## Efficiency

`wiremock` maintains a pool of mock servers in the background to minimise the number of
connections and the time spent starting up a new [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html).
Pooling reduces the likelihood of you having to tune your OS configurations (e.g. ulimit).

The pool is designed to be invisible: it makes your life easier and your tests faster. If you end up having to worry about it, it's a bug: open an issue!

## Prior art

[ mockito](https://docs.rs/mockito/) and

[provide HTTP mocking for Rust.](https://docs.rs/httpmock/)

`httpmock`Check the table below to see how `wiremock` compares to them across the following dimensions:

- Test execution strategy (do tests have to be executed sequentially or can they be executed in parallel?);
- How many APIs can I mock in a test?
- Out-of-the-box request matchers;
- Extensible request matching (i.e. you can define your own matchers);
- Sync/Async API;
- Spying (e.g. verify that a mock has/hasn't been called in a test);
- Standalone mode (i.e. can I launch an HTTP mock server outside of a test suite?).

| Test execution strategy | How many APIs can I mock? | Out-of-the-box request matchers | Extensible request maching | API | Spying | Standalone mode | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mockito | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ❌ |
| httpmock | ✔ Parallel | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async/Sync | ✔ | ✔ |
| wiremock | ✔ Parallel ️ | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async | ✔ | ❌ |

## Future evolution

More request matchers can be added to those provided out-of-the-box to handle common usecases.

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in this crate by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.0/wiremock/struct.MockBuilder.html#method.respond_with)

`respond_with`You also given the option to have [ Mock](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.0/wiremock/struct.Mock.html)s that return different responses based on the matched

[using the](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.0/wiremock/struct.Request)

`Request`[trait.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.0/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`Check

['s documentation for more details and examples.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.0/wiremock/trait.Respond.html)

`Respond`## Test isolation

Each instance of [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.0/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) is fully isolated:

[takes care of finding a random port available on your local machine which is assigned to the new](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.0/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html#method.start)

`start`[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.0/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`You should use one instance of [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.0/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) for each test, to ensure full isolation and
no cross-test interference.

When a [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.0/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance goes out of scope (e.g. the test finishes), the corresponding
HTTP server running in the background is shut down to free up the port it was using.

## Runtime compatibility

`wiremock` can be used (and it is tested to work) with both [ async_std](https://docs.rs/async-std/) and

[as futures runtimes. If you encounter any compatibility bug, please open an issue on our](https://docs.rs/tokio/)

`tokio`[GitHub repository](https://github.com/LukeMathWalker/wiremock-rs).

## Efficiency

`wiremock` maintains a pool of mock servers in the background to minimise the number of
connections and the time spent starting up a new [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.4.0/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html).

Pooling reduces the likelihood of you having to tune your OS configurations (e.g. ulimit).

The pool is designed to be invisible: it makes your life easier and your tests faster. If you end up having to worry about it, it's a bug: open an issue!

## Prior art

[ mockito](https://docs.rs/mockito/) and

[provide HTTP mocking for Rust.](https://docs.rs/httpmock/)

`httpmock`Check the table below to see how `wiremock` compares to them across the following dimensions:

- Test execution strategy (do tests have to be executed sequentially or can they be executed in parallel?);
- How many APIs can I mock in a test?
- Out-of-the-box request matchers;
- Extensible request matching (i.e. you can define your own matchers);
- Sync/Async API;
- Spying (e.g. verify that a mock has/hasn't been called in a test);
- Standalone mode (i.e. can I launch an HTTP mock server outside of a test suite?).

| Test execution strategy | How many APIs can I mock? | Out-of-the-box request matchers | Extensible request maching | API | Spying | Standalone mode | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mockito | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ❌ |
| httpmock | ✔ Parallel | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async/Sync | ✔ | ✔ |
| wiremock | ✔ Parallel ️ | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async | ✔ | ❌ |

## Future evolution

More request matchers can be added to those provided out-of-the-box to handle common usecases.

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in this crate by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

`start`[.](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.2.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`You should use one instance of [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.2.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) for each test, to ensure full isolation and
no cross-test interference.

When a [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.2.4/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance goes out of scope (e.g. the test finishes), the corresponding
HTTP server running in the background is shut down to free up the port it was using.

## Runtime compatibility

`wiremock` can be used (and it is tested to work) with both [ async_std](https://docs.rs/async-std/) and

[as futures runtimes. If you encounter any compatibility bug, please open an issue on our](https://docs.rs/tokio/)

`tokio`[GitHub repository](https://github.com/LukeMathWalker/wiremock-rs).

## Prior art

[ mockito](https://docs.rs/mockito/) and

[provide HTTP mocking for Rust.](https://docs.rs/httpmock/)

`httpmock`Check the table below to see how `wiremock` compares to them across the following dimensions:

- Test execution strategy (do tests have to be executed sequentially or can they be executed in parallel?);
- How many APIs can I mock in a test?
- Out-of-the-box request matchers;
- Extensible request matching (i.e. you can define your own matchers);
- Sync/Async API;
- Spying (e.g. verify that a mock has/hasn't been called in a test);
- Standalone mode (i.e. can I launch an HTTP mock server outside of a test suite?).

| Test execution strategy | How many APIs can I mock? | Out-of-the-box request matchers | Extensible request maching | API | Spying | Standalone mode | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mockito | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ❌ |
| httpmock | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ✔ |
| wiremock | ✔ Parallel ️ | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async | ✔ | ❌ |

## Future evolution

More request matchers can be added to those provided out-of-the-box to handle common usecases.

no cross-test interference.

When a [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/wiremock/0.1.0/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html) instance goes out of scope (e.g. the test finishes), the corresponding
HTTP server running in the background is shut down to free up the port it was using.

## Runtime compatibility

`wiremock` can be used (and it is tested to work) with both [ async_std](https://docs.rs/async-std/) and

[as futures runtimes.](https://docs.rs/tokio/)

`tokio`If you encounter any compatibility bug, please open an issue on our

[GitHub repository](https://github.com/LukeMathWalker/wiremock-rs).

## Prior art

[ mockito](https://docs.rs/mockito/) and

[provide HTTP mocking for Rust.](https://docs.rs/httpmock/)

`httpmock`Check the table below to see how `wiremock` compares to them across the following dimensions:

- Test execution strategy (do tests have to be executed sequentially or can they be executed in parallel?);
- How many APIs can I mock in a test?
- Out-of-the-box request matchers;
- Extensible request matching (i.e. you can define your own matchers);
- Sync/Async API;
- Spying (e.g. verify that a mock has/hasn't been called in a test);
- Standalone mode (i.e. can I launch an HTTP mock server outside of a test suite?).

| Test execution strategy | How many APIs can I mock? | Out-of-the-box request matchers | Extensible request maching | API | Spying | Standalone mode | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mockito | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ❌ |
| httpmock | ❌ Sequential | ❌ 1 | ✔ | ❌ | Sync | ✔ | ✔ |
| wiremock | ✔ Parallel ️ | ✔ Unbounded | ✔ | ✔ | Async | ❌ | ❌ |

## Future evolution

Spying is in scope for future releases of `wiremock`.

More request matchers can be added to those provided out-of-the-box to handle common usecases.

# wiremock::matchers - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/matchers/index.html

## Expand description

A collection of different matching strategies provided out-of-the-box by `wiremock`.

If the set of matchers provided out-of-the-box is not enough for your specific testing needs
you can implement your own thanks to the [ Match](https://docs.rs/trait.Match.html) trait.

Furthermore, `Fn` closures that take an immutable [ Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html) reference as input and return a boolean
as input automatically implement

[and can be used where a matcher is expected.](https://docs.rs/trait.Match.html)

`Match`Check [ Match](https://docs.rs/trait.Match.html)’s documentation for examples.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [AnyMatcher](https://docs.rs/struct.AnyMatcher.html)
- Match all incoming requests, regardless of their method, path, headers or body.
- [Basic](https://docs.rs/struct.BasicAuthMatcher.html)- Auth - Matcher
- Match an incoming request if it contains the basic authentication header with the username and password
as per [RFC 7617](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7617).
- [Bearer](https://docs.rs/struct.BearerTokenMatcher.html)- Token - Matcher
- Match an incoming request if it contains the bearer token header
as per [RFC 6750](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750).
- [Body](https://docs.rs/struct.BodyContainsMatcher.html)- Contains - Matcher
- Match part of the body of a request.
- [Body](https://docs.rs/struct.BodyExactMatcher.html)- Exact - Matcher
- Match **exactly**the body of a request.
- [Body](https://docs.rs/struct.BodyPartialJsonMatcher.html)- Partial - Json - Matcher
- Match part JSON body of a request.
- [Header](https://docs.rs/struct.HeaderExactMatcher.html)- Exact - Matcher
- Match **exactly**the header of a request.
- [Header](https://docs.rs/struct.HeaderExistsMatcher.html)- Exists - Matcher
- Match **exactly**the header name of a request. It checks that the header is present but does not validate the value.
- [Header](https://docs.rs/struct.HeaderRegexMatcher.html)- Regex - Matcher
- Match the value of a header using a regular expression. If the header is multi-valued, all values must satisfy the regular expression. If the header is missing, the mock will not match.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/struct.MethodExactMatcher.html)- Exact - Matcher
- Match **exactly**the method of a request.
- [Path](https://docs.rs/struct.PathExactMatcher.html)- Exact - Matcher
- Match **exactly**the path of a request.
- [Path](https://docs.rs/struct.PathRegexMatcher.html)- Regex - Matcher
- Match the path of a request against a regular expression.
- [Query](https://docs.rs/struct.QueryParamContainsMatcher.html)- Param - Contains - Matcher
- Match when a query parameter contains the specified value as a substring.
- [Query](https://docs.rs/struct.QueryParamExactMatcher.html)- Param - Exact - Matcher
- Match **exactly**the query parameter of a request.
- [Query](https://docs.rs/struct.QueryParamIsMissingMatcher.html)- Param - IsMissing - Matcher
- Only match requests that do **not**contain a specified query parameter.

# Match in wiremock - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/trait.Match.html

## Expand description

Anything that implements `Match` can be used to constrain when a [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html) is activated.

`Match` can be used to extend the set of matchers provided out-of-the-box by `wiremock` to
cater to your specific testing needs:

```
use wiremock::{Match, MockServer, Mock, Request, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::HeaderExactMatcher;
use std::convert::TryInto;
// Check that a header with the specified name exists and its value has an odd length.
pub struct OddHeaderMatcher(http::HeaderName);
impl Match for OddHeaderMatcher {
    fn matches(&self, request: &Request) -> bool {
        match request.headers.get(&self.0) {
            // We are ignoring multi-valued headers for simplicity
            Some(value) => value.to_str().unwrap_or_default().len() % 2 == 1,
            None => false
        }
    }
}
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    Mock::given(OddHeaderMatcher("custom".try_into().unwrap()))
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200))
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;
    let client = reqwest::Client::new();
    // Even length
    let status = client
        .get(&mock_server.uri())
        .header("custom", "even")
        .send()
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 404);
    // Odd length
    let status = client
        .get(&mock_server.uri())
        .header("custom", "odd")
        .send()
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 200);
}
```
Anonymous functions that take a reference to a [ Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html) as input and return a boolean
as output automatically implement the

`Match` trait.The previous example could be rewritten as follows:

```
use wiremock::{Match, MockServer, Mock, Request, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::HeaderExactMatcher;
use std::convert::TryInto;
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;

    let header_name = http::HeaderName::from_static("custom");
    // Check that a header with the specified name exists and its value has an odd length.
    let matcher = move |request: &Request| {
        match request.headers.get(&header_name) {
            Some(value) => value.to_str().unwrap_or_default().len() % 2 == 1,
            None => false
        }
    };
    Mock::given(matcher)
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200))
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;
    let client = reqwest::Client::new();
    // Even length
    let status = client
        .get(&mock_server.uri())
        .header("custom", "even")
        .send()
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 404);
    // Odd length
    let status = client
        .get(&mock_server.uri())
        .header("custom", "odd")
        .send()
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 200);
}
```

# Mock in wiremock - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Mock.html

`pub struct Mock { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Given a set of matchers, a `Mock` instructs an instance of [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html) to return a pre-determined response if the matching conditions are satisfied.

`Mock`s have to be mounted (or registered) with a [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html) to become effective.
You can use:

- `MockServer::register`- `Mock::mount`- **global**- `Mock`;
- `MockServer::register_as_scoped`- `Mock::mount_as_scoped`- **scoped**- `Mock`.

Check the respective documentations for more details (or look at the following examples!).

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    let response = ResponseTemplate::new(200);
    let mock = Mock::given(method("GET")).respond_with(response.clone());
    // Registering the mock with the mock server - it's now effective!
    mock_server.register(mock).await;
    // We won't register this mock instead.
    let unregistered_mock = Mock::given(method("POST")).respond_with(response);

    // Act
    let status = reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 200);
    // This would have matched `unregistered_mock`, but we haven't registered it!
    // Hence it returns a 404, the default response when no mocks matched on the mock server.
    let client = reqwest::Client::new();
    let status = client.post(&mock_server.uri())
        .send()
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 404);
}
```
If you prefer a fluent style, you can use the [ mount](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html#method.mount) method on the

`Mock` itself
instead of [.](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html#method.register)

`register````
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    Mock::given(method("GET"))
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200))
        .up_to_n_times(1)
        // Mounting the mock on the mock server - it's now effective!
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;

    // Act
    let status = reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 200);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-using-mount_as_scoped)Example (using `mount_as_scoped`

`mount_as_scoped`Sometimes you will need a `Mock` to be active within the scope of a function, but not any longer.
You can use [ Mock::mount_as_scoped](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html#method.mount_as_scoped) to precisely control how long a

`Mock` stays active.```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
async fn my_test_helper(mock_server: &MockServer) {
    let mock_guard = Mock::given(method("GET"))
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200))
        .expect(1)
        .named("my_test_helper GET /")
        .mount_as_scoped(mock_server)
        .await;
    reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap();
    // `mock_guard` is dropped, expectations are verified!
}
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    my_test_helper(&mock_server).await;
    // Act
    // This would have returned 200 if the `Mock` in
    // `my_test_helper` had not been scoped.
    let status = reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 404);
}
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wiremock/mock.rs.html#354-358)#### pub fn [up_to_n_times](https://docs.rs#method.up_to_n_times)(self, n: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)) -> [Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wiremock/mock.rs.html#354-358)

#### pub fn [up_to_n_times](https://docs.rs#method.up_to_n_times)(self, n: [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)) -> [Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)

Specify an upper limit to the number of times you would like this [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html) to respond to
incoming requests that satisfy the conditions imposed by your

[.](https://docs.rs/matchers/index.html)

`matchers`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example:

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    Mock::given(method("GET"))
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200))
        // Default behaviour will have this Mock responding to any incoming request
        // that satisfied our matcher (e.g. being a GET request).
        // We can opt out of the default behaviour by setting a cap on the number of
        // matching requests this Mock should respond to.
        //
        // In this case, once one matching request has been received, the mock will stop
        // matching additional requests and you will receive a 404 if no other mock
        // matches on those requests.
        .up_to_n_times(1)
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;

    // Act
    // The first request matches, as expected.
    let status = reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 200);
    // The second request does NOT match given our `up_to_n_times(1)` setting.
    let status = reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 404);
}
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wiremock/mock.rs.html#405-409)#### pub fn [with_priority](https://docs.rs#method.with_priority)(self, p: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)) -> [Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wiremock/mock.rs.html#405-409)

#### pub fn [with_priority](https://docs.rs#method.with_priority)(self, p: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)) -> [Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)

Specify a priority for this [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html).
Use this when you mount many

[in a](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock`[and those mocks have interlaced request matching conditions e.g.](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer``mock A` accepts path `/abcd` and `mock B` a path regex `[a-z]{4}`
It is recommended to set the highest priority (1) for mocks with exact conditions (`mock A` in this case)
`1` is the highest priority, `255` the lowest, default to `5`
If two mocks have the same priority, priority is defined by insertion order (first one mounted has precedence over the others).[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example:

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::{method, path, path_regex};
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    Mock::given(method("GET"))
        .and(path("abcd"))
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200))
        .with_priority(1) // highest priority
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;
    Mock::given(method("GET"))
        .and(path_regex("[a-z]{4}"))
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(201))
        .with_priority(2)
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;
    // Act
    // The request with highest priority, as expected.
    let status = reqwest::get(&format!("{}/abcd", mock_server.uri()))
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 200);
}
```
Set an expectation on the number of times this [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html) should match in the current
test case.
Expectations are verified when the

[is shutting down: if the expectation is not satisfied, the](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`[will panic and the](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer``error_message` is shown.By default, no expectation is set for [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)s.

[§](https://docs.rs#when-is-this-useful)When is this useful?

`expect` can turn out handy when you’d like to verify that a certain side-effect has
(or has not!) taken place.

For example:

- check that a 3rd party notification API (e.g. email service) is called when an event in your application is supposed to trigger a notification;
- check that a 3rd party API is NOT called when the response of a call is expected
to be retrieved from a cache (`.expect(0)`).

This technique is also called [spying](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/TestDouble.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example:

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    Mock::given(method("GET"))
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200))
        .up_to_n_times(2)
        // We expect the mock to be called at least once.
        // If that does not happen, the `MockServer` will panic on shutdown,
        // causing the whole test to fail.
        .expect(1..)
        // We assign a name to the mock - it will be shown in error messages
        // if our expectation is not verified!
        .named("Root GET")
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;

    // Act
    let status = reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 200);
    // Assert
    // We made at least one matching request, the expectation is satisfied.
    // The `MockServer` will shutdown peacefully, without panicking.
}
```
Assign a name to your mock.

The mock name will be used in error messages (e.g. if the mock expectation is not satisfied) and debug logs to help you identify what failed.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    // We have two mocks in the same test - how do we find out
    // which one failed when the test panics?
    // Assigning a name to each mock with `named` gives us better error
    // messages and makes it much easier to debug why a test is failing!
    Mock::given(method("GET"))
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200))
        .up_to_n_times(2)
        .expect(1..)
        // We assign a name to the mock - it will be shown in error messages
        // if our expectation is not verified!
        .named("Root GET")
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;
    Mock::given(method("POST"))
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200))
        .up_to_n_times(2)
        .expect(1..)
        // We assign a name to the mock - it will be shown in error messages
        // if our expectation is not verified!
        .named("Root POST")
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;

    // Act
    let status = reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 200);
    // Assert
    // We did not make a POST request, therefore the expectation on `Root POST`
    // is not satisfied and the test will panic.
}
```

Mount a [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html) as

**scoped**on an instance of

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`When using [ mount](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html#method.mount), your

[s will be active until the](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)

`MockServer`When using

`Mock`[is not dropped. When the returned](https://docs.rs/struct.MockGuard.html)

`MockGuard`[is dropped,](https://docs.rs/struct.MockGuard.html)

`MockGuard`[will verify that the expectations set on the scoped](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`[were verified - if not, it will panic.](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock``mount_as_scoped` is the ideal solution when you need a [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html) within a test helper
but you do not want it to linger around after the end of the function execution.

[§](https://docs.rs#limitations)Limitations

When expectations of a scoped [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html) are not verified, it will trigger a panic - just like a normal

[. Due to](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock`[limitations](https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/should-drop-glue-use-track-caller/13682)in Rust’s

[trait, the panic message will not include the filename and the line location where the corresponding](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/drop/trait.Drop.html)

`Drop`[was dropped - it will point into](https://docs.rs/struct.MockGuard.html)

`MockGuard``wiremock`’s source code.This can be an issue when you are using more than one scoped [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html) in a single test - which of them panicked?

To improve your debugging experience it is strongly recommended to use

[to assign a unique identifier to your scoped](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html#method.named)

`Mock::named`[s, which will in turn be referenced in the panic message if their expectations are not met.](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock`[§](https://docs.rs#example-4)Example:

- The behaviour of the scoped mock is invisible outside of `my_test_helper`.

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
async fn my_test_helper(mock_server: &MockServer) {
    let mock_guard = Mock::given(method("GET"))
        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200))
        .expect(1)
        .named("my_test_helper GET /")
        .mount_as_scoped(mock_server)
        .await;
    reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap();
    // `mock_guard` is dropped, expectations are verified!
}
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    my_test_helper(&mock_server).await;
    // Act
    // This would have returned 200 if the `Mock` in
    // `my_test_helper` had not been scoped.
    let status = reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 404);
}
```
- The expectations for the scoped mock are not verified, it panics at the end of `my_test_helper`.

# MockServer in wiremock - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.MockServer.html

`pub struct MockServer(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

An HTTP web-server running in the background to behave as one of your dependencies using [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)s
for testing purposes.

Each instance of `MockServer` is fully isolated: [ MockServer::start](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html#method.start) takes care of finding a random port
available on your local machine which is assigned to the new

`MockServer`.You can use [ MockServer::builder](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html#method.builder) if you need to specify custom configuration - e.g.
run on a specific port or disable request recording.

[§](https://docs.rs#best-practices)Best practices

You should use one instance of `MockServer` for each REST API that your application interacts
with and needs mocking for testing purposes.

To ensure full isolation and no cross-test interference, `MockServer`s shouldn’t be
shared between tests. Instead, `MockServer`s should be created in the test where they are used.

When using a [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html) within a test helper function, consider using

[instead of](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html#method.register_as_scoped)

`MockServer::register_as_scoped`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html#method.register)

`MockServer::register`You can register as many [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)s as your scenario requires on a

`MockServer`.## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wiremock/mock_server/exposed_server.rs.html#58-487)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-MockServer)### impl [MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)

### impl [MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)

Start a new instance of a `MockServer` listening on a random port.

Each instance of `MockServer` is fully isolated: `start` takes care of finding a random port
available on your local machine which is assigned to the new `MockServer`.

You should use one instance of `MockServer` for each REST API that your application interacts
with and needs mocking for testing purposes.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example:

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server_one = MockServer::start().await;
    let mock_server_two = MockServer::start().await;
    assert!(mock_server_one.address() != mock_server_two.address());
    let mock = Mock::given(method("GET")).respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200));
    // Registering the mock with the first mock server - it's now effective!
    // But it *won't* be used by the second mock server!
    mock_server_one.register(mock).await;
    // Act
    let status = reqwest::get(&mock_server_one.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 200);
    // This would have matched our mock, but we haven't registered it for `mock_server_two`!
    // Hence it returns a 404, the default response when no mocks matched on the mock server.
    let status = reqwest::get(&mock_server_two.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 404);
}
```
Register a [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html) on an instance of

`MockServer`.The

[will remain active until](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock``MockServer` is shut down. If you want to control or limit how
long your [stays active, check out](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)

`Mock`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html#method.register_as_scoped)

`MockServer::register_as_scoped`Be careful! [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)s are not effective until they are

[ed or](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html#method.mount)

`mount``register`ed on a `MockServer`.
`register` is an asynchronous method, make sure to `.await` it![§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example:

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    let response = ResponseTemplate::new(200);
    let mock = Mock::given(method("GET")).respond_with(response.clone());
    // Registering the mock with the mock server - it's now effective!
    mock_server.register(mock).await;
    // We won't register this mock instead.
    let unregistered_mock = Mock::given(method("GET")).respond_with(response);
    // Act
    let status = reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 200);
    // This would have matched `unregistered_mock`, but we haven't registered it!
    // Hence it returns a 404, the default response when no mocks matched on the mock server.
    let client = reqwest::Client::new();
    let status = client.post(&mock_server.uri())
        .send()
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 404);
}
```

`Mock``register_as_scoped` is the ideal solution when you need a [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html) within a test helper

Drop all mounted [ Mock](https://docs.rs/struct.Mock.html)s from an instance of

[. It also deletes all recorded requests.](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html)

`MockServer`[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    let response = ResponseTemplate::new(200);
    Mock::given(method("GET")).respond_with(response).mount(&mock_server).await;
    // Act
    let status = reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 200);
    // Reset the server
    mock_server.reset().await;
    // This would have matched our mock, but we have dropped it resetting the server!
    let client = reqwest::Client::new();
    let status = client.post(&mock_server.uri())
        .send()
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .status();
    assert_eq!(status, 404);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example-recorded-requests-are-reset)Example (Recorded requests are reset)

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    // Act
    reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri()).await.unwrap();
    // We have recorded the incoming request
    let received_requests = mock_server.received_requests().await.unwrap();
    assert!(!received_requests.is_empty());
    // Reset the server
    mock_server.reset().await;
    // All received requests have been forgotten after the call to `.reset`
    let received_requests = mock_server.received_requests().await.unwrap();
    assert!(received_requests.is_empty())
}
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wiremock/mock_server/exposed_server.rs.html#484-486)#### pub async fn [received_requests](https://docs.rs#method.received_requests)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html)>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wiremock/mock_server/exposed_server.rs.html#484-486)

#### pub async fn [received_requests](https://docs.rs#method.received_requests)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html)>>

Return a vector with all the requests received by the `MockServer` since it started.
If no request has been served, it returns an empty vector.

If request recording has been disabled using [ MockServerBuilder::disable_request_recording](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServerBuilder.html#method.disable_request_recording),
it returns

`None`.[§](https://docs.rs#example-6)Example:

```
use wiremock::MockServer;
use http::Method;
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    // Act
    reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri()).await.unwrap();
    // Assert
    let received_requests = mock_server.received_requests().await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(received_requests.len(), 1);
    let received_request = &received_requests[0];
    assert_eq!(received_request.method, Method::GET);
    assert_eq!(received_request.url.path(), "/");
    assert!(received_request.body.is_empty());
}

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Start building a `ResponseTemplate` specifying the status code of the response.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wiremock/response_template.rs.html#52-65)#### pub fn [append_header](https://docs.rs#method.append_header)<K, V>(self, key: K, value: V) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wiremock/response_template.rs.html#52-65)

#### pub fn [append_header](https://docs.rs#method.append_header)<K, V>(self, key: K, value: V) -> Self

Append a header `value` to list of headers with `key` as header name.

Unlike `insert_header`, this function will not override the contents of a header:

- if there are no header values with `key`as header name, it will insert one;
- if there are already some values with `key`as header name, it will append to the existing list.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wiremock/response_template.rs.html#102-115)#### pub fn [insert_header](https://docs.rs#method.insert_header)<K, V>(self, key: K, value: V) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wiremock/response_template.rs.html#102-115)

#### pub fn [insert_header](https://docs.rs#method.insert_header)<K, V>(self, key: K, value: V) -> Self

Insert a header `value` with `key` as header name.

This function will override the contents of a header:

- if there are no header values with `key`as header name, it will insert one;
- if there are already some values with `key`as header name, it will drop them and start a new list of header values, containing only`value`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example:

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    let correlation_id = "1311db4f-fe65-4cb2-b514-1bb47f781aa7";
    let template = ResponseTemplate::new(200).insert_header(
        "X-Correlation-ID",
        correlation_id
    );
    Mock::given(method("GET"))
        .respond_with(template)
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;
    // Act
    let res = reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap();
    // Assert
    assert_eq!(res.headers().get("X-Correlation-ID").unwrap().to_str().unwrap(), correlation_id);
}
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wiremock/response_template.rs.html#256-265)#### pub fn [set_body_raw](https://docs.rs#method.set_body_raw)<B>(self, body: B, mime: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/wiremock/response_template.rs.html#256-265)

#### pub fn [set_body_raw](https://docs.rs#method.set_body_raw)<B>(self, body: B, mime: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> Self

Set a raw response body. The mime type needs to be set because the raw body could be of any type.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example:

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
mod external {
    // This could be a method of a struct that is
    // implemented in another crate and the struct
    // does not implement Serialize.
    pub fn body() -> Vec<u8>{
        r#"{"hello": "world"}"#.as_bytes().to_owned()
    }
}
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    let template = ResponseTemplate::new(200).set_body_raw(
        external::body(),
        "application/json"
    );
    Mock::given(method("GET"))
        .respond_with(template)
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;
    // Act
    let mut res = reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
        .await
        .unwrap();
    let content_type = res.headers().get(reqwest::header::CONTENT_TYPE).cloned();
    let body = res.text()
        .await
        .unwrap();
    // Assert
    assert_eq!(body, r#"{"hello": "world"}"#);
    assert_eq!(content_type, Some("application/json".parse().unwrap()));
}
```
By default the [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html) tries to fulfill incoming requests as fast as possible.

You can use `set_delay` to introduce an artificial delay to simulate the behaviour of
a real server with a non-negligible latency.

In particular, you can use it to test the behaviour of your timeout policies.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example:

```
use wiremock::{MockServer, Mock, ResponseTemplate};
use wiremock::matchers::method;
use std::time::Duration;
use async_std::prelude::FutureExt;
#[async_std::main]
async fn main() {
    // Arrange
    let mock_server = MockServer::start().await;
    let delay = Duration::from_secs(1);
    let template = ResponseTemplate::new(200).set_delay(delay);
    Mock::given(method("GET"))
        .respond_with(template)
        .mount(&mock_server)
        .await;
    // Act
    let mut res = async_std::future::timeout(
        // Shorter than the response delay!
        delay / 3,
        reqwest::get(&mock_server.uri())
    )
    .await;
    // Assert - Timeout error!
    assert!(res.is_err());
}
```

# Request in wiremock - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wiremock/latest/wiremock/struct.Request.html

## Expand description

An incoming request to an instance of [ MockServer](https://docs.rs/struct.MockServer.html).

Each matcher gets an immutable reference to a `Request` instance in the [ matches](https://docs.rs/trait.Match.html#tymethod.matches) method
defined in the

[trait.](https://docs.rs/trait.Match.html)

`Match`[§](https://docs.rs#implementation-notes)Implementation notes:

We can’t use `http_types::Request` directly in our `Match::matches` signature:
it requires having mutable access to the request to extract the body (which gets
consumed when read!).
It would also require `matches` to be async, which is cumbersome due to the lack of async traits.

We introduce our `Request` type to perform this extraction once when the request
arrives in the mock serve, store the result and pass an immutable reference to it
to all our matchers.
